summary: This Dockerfile creates a minimal Python 3.13 container with DuckDB CLI installed. It sets up environment variables to optimize Python's behavior in containers, downloads and installs the DuckDB command-line tool from GitHub, creates a non-root user called 'developer' for security, and configures the container to run DuckDB as the default command.

explanations.1: This special comment tells Docker to use an experimental syntax version that enables advanced features like heredocs and other modern Dockerfile capabilities.
explanations.5: These environment variables tell Python not to create .pyc cache files, to print output immediately instead of buffering, and to skip checking for pip updates — all good practices for containers.
explanations.9: These ARG lines define build-time variables that can be passed in when building (like `docker build --build-arg UID=2000`), allowing customization without editing the file.
explanations.15: The RUN command chains multiple shell commands with && so they all run in one layer; if any command fails, the whole thing stops instead of continuing.
explanations.17: The curl flags mean: fail on errors (-f), silently suppress progress (-s), show errors (-S), and follow redirects (-L); the pipe (|) feeds curl's output directly to tar without writing to disk first.
explanations.21: Deleting the apt cache files after installing packages shrinks the final image size significantly since we don't need those files at runtime.
explanations.23: This creates a Unix group and user called 'developer' with specific numeric IDs; the nologin shell prevents anyone from logging in as this user interactively.
explanations.28: This switches from running as root to running as the 'developer' user, so the container won't have unnecessary privileges.
